statements.status_notes: An excessive number of attachment headers can cause uncontrolled resource consumption while CXF deserializes a message. The Open Liberty security table identifies 26.0.0.8 as the fixed product release for this CVE. This image ships the later IBM Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 runtime from its checksum-pinned, signature-verified release archive without replacing the vendor bundles. The observed CXF PURLs retain source/POM base versions of code in those vendor-rebuilt bundles; they do not indicate an unpatched standalone upstream installation. The vendor remediation therefore already exists in this product payload. This assessment is scoped to this Open Liberty image and does not assess arbitrary artifacts with the same base PURL. Vendor fixed-release record: https://openliberty.io/docs/latest/security-vulnerabilities.html. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ghvc-7hp8-2g2v.

Vendor fixed-release record: https://openliberty.io/docs/latest/security-vulnerabilities.html. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xw5h-cmh3-8j6j.

A CXF logging path can read an entire cached temporary file into memory and log it, enabling memory exhaustion and exposing cached plaintext even when temporary-file encryption is configured. The logging path, message control and any vendor-specific correction in these bundled components remain unverified. Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 ships this code inside vendor-assembled bundles. Changing a standalone library dependency does not replace that bundled implementation; a compatible vendor release or validated bundle remediation and application-specific applicability assessment remain unresolved. A base-version scanner match alone does not establish exploitability. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-36wv-v2qp-v4g4.

Aegis DataBinding can permit server-side request forgery while processing webservice parameters; other bindings, including the default binding, are excluded by the advisory. The primary affected package is cxf-rt-databinding-aegis, while the scanner maps cxf-core base versions. Whether that Aegis implementation and configuration are used in this vendor payload remains unverified. Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 ships this code inside vendor-assembled bundles. Changing a standalone library dependency does not replace that bundled implementation; a compatible vendor release or validated bundle remediation and application-specific applicability assessment remain unresolved. A base-version scanner match alone does not establish exploitability. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qmgx-j96g-4428.

A CXFServlet configured with both static-resources-list and redirect-query-check can expose directory listings or source content. The advisory requires that particular misconfiguration. The servlet mapping, resource policy and any vendor-specific remediation in this payload remain unverified. Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 ships this code inside vendor-assembled bundles. Changing a standalone library dependency does not replace that bundled implementation; a compatible vendor release or validated bundle remediation and application-specific applicability assessment remain unresolved. A base-version scanner match alone does not establish exploitability. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3w37-5p3p-jv92.

JwtRequestCodeFilter can fetch a JWT from an insufficiently validated request_uri, enabling denial of service against an authorization service. The scanner maps CXF core, JAX-RS frontend and HTTP transport base components. Whether Liberty applications use that OAuth filter and accept the relevant untrusted URI remains unverified. Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 ships this code inside vendor-assembled bundles. Changing a standalone library dependency does not replace that bundled implementation; a compatible vendor release or validated bundle remediation and application-specific applicability assessment remain unresolved. A base-version scanner match alone does not establish exploitability. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7q4h-pj78-j7vg.

CXF JMX integration can permit a same-host registry rebinding attack when the InstrumentationManager connector factory is enabled. The primary advisory names cxf-rt-management, while the scanner associates this finding with cxf-core 3.1.18. The exact management-component relationship and configured JMX connector path remain unverified; this is not a confirmed vulnerability in every use of cxf-core. Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 ships this code inside vendor-assembled bundles. Changing a standalone library dependency does not replace that bundled implementation; a compatible vendor release or validated bundle remediation and application-specific applicability assessment remain unresolved. A base-version scanner match alone does not establish exploitability. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ffm7-7r8g-77xm.

The CXF /services listing can reflect a malicious styleSheetPath into a page, enabling cross-site scripting. The scanner associates the CXF core, JAX-RS frontend and HTTP transport base components with this report. Whether the affected service-list page and parameter handling are exposed by configured Liberty applications remains unverified. Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 ships this code inside vendor-assembled bundles. Changing a standalone library dependency does not replace that bundled implementation; a compatible vendor release or validated bundle remediation and application-specific applicability assessment remain unresolved. A base-version scanner match alone does not establish exploitability. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-64x2-gq24-75pv.

The CXF OpenID Connect JWK service can disclose private or secret keys when a JWK keystore file containing those keys is returned without the required filtering. Ordinary JKS/PKCS12 keystores are excluded by the advisory. The scanner maps the broader CXF base to cxf-core; the relevant JWK service component and keystore configuration in this vendor payload remain unverified. Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 ships this code inside vendor-assembled bundles. Changing a standalone library dependency does not replace that bundled implementation; a compatible vendor release or validated bundle remediation and application-specific applicability assessment remain unresolved. A base-version scanner match alone does not establish exploitability. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-42f2-f9vc-6365.
